experiments.result: the ER gains are spread over the catalogue rather than carried by a few items (4.8-5.6% of the held-out anchors changed, and the top 1% of anchors carry 18-21% of the change), the code cells are the same size as the control's for the geometry arm (102 vs 103) and larger for the residual target (111), and the downstream differences are 2.1 and 9.3 times the Stage-3 run-to-run band
experiments.verdict: the ER gain is not a concentration artefact, and the geometry arm's export is not degraded; the downstream difference is real but small for the geometry arm and clearly negative for the residual target

predictions.falsifier: Per-item ER changes are broadly distributed across the catalogue and not dominated by a small subset.

predictions.statement: ER improvements are highly concentrated, with many items unchanged or worse and a small fraction accounting for most of the aggregate gain.

explanations.statement: The ER gain is concentrated in a small subset of items or transitions, so catalogue-wide recommendation opportunities barely change.

predictions.falsifier: Neighbourhood-span and prefix-distribution metrics are unchanged or improve, and candidate recall under the same beam-search procedure does not decline.

explanations.statement: The changed codes have less useful neighbourhood and prefix structure for beam search, even where pair-level ER improves.

predictions.falsifier: Cross-seed SID agreement and level-wise assignment stability are at least as high as control.

predictions.statement: Treatment codes show lower cross-seed item-level SID agreement or less consistent level-wise assignments than control, even when their aggregate ER is favorable.

explanations.statement: The pair-level ER hides instability across training seeds or across the three code levels, making the treatment's codes unreliable for downstream retrieval.

predictions.falsifier: A repeated-seed comparison shows a consistent treatment effect whose uncertainty interval excludes zero.

predictions.statement: Across repeated Stage-3 training seeds, treatment and control recall@10 distributions overlap substantially and the estimated treatment-control difference is not distinguishable from seed variability.

explanations.statement: The apparent Stage-3 differences are within run-to-run noise of the Stage-3 trainer rather than a reliable treatment effect.

hypotheses.notes: the ER gain is broad and the export is not damaged, yet the downstream quality did not follow; the pair-level ER and the recommender's objective are decoupled on this host. FIVE arms have now cleared the gate (ER 16.4028, 16.5034, 16.5918, 16.6160, 16.6516) and NONE improved the downstream metric (recall@10 0.062257, 0.061004, 0.063737, 0.063389, 0.062414 against the archived control's 0.064068). The two explanations the executed experiments could test are ruled out; the remaining one -- that the pair-level ER and the recommender's objective measure different things -- stands, and this issue does not settle it
hypotheses.observation: stage2-behavior_conditioned_pairwise_curvature-20261021T082026 had Hard-L1 ER 2.619839290662233, while stage2-behaviour_conditioned_residual_target-20261021T082030 and stage2-behavior_residual_geometry_transport-20261021T082034 had ERs above the control gate and Stage-3 recall@10 below control-r8_control-20261021T082024.

experiments.result: the residual target concentrates the level-0 usage (Gini +0.137, entropy -0.137) and loses 4.8% of its level-2 occupancy; the geometry transport arm leaves the balance essentially unchanged (Gini +0.012, entropy -0.0005) and improves its train-over-held-out discrimination ratio by 4.5%
experiments.verdict: the residual target's ER gain was bought with a more concentrated level-0 code distribution, which is consistent with its downstream regression; the geometry arm's export is healthy and generalises, so its flat downstream result is not explained by the code distribution or by overfitting

predictions.falsifier: Across the available artifacts, ER improvement consistently predicts improved Stage-3 candidate ranking and retrieval.

predictions.statement: Across items and held-out transitions, changes in ER will have weak or inconsistent association with changes in Stage-3-relevant candidate ranking or retrieval, including cases where ER improves but candidate ranking worsens.

predictions.falsifier: Artifacts that pass the ER gate also consistently preserve or improve Stage-3 candidate recall under matched evaluation.

predictions.statement: The ER-only gate admits artifacts that fail a direct Stage-3 candidate-retrieval check.

explanations.statement: The ER admission signal is not aligned with the downstream recommendation objective: pair-level separation can improve without preserving the item geometry or ranking information that Stage-3 needs.

experiments.result: in a matched pair on the host's own mini case, an auxiliary term changes the encoder gradient by 1.66e-05 before the host's post-backward assembly and by exactly 0.0 after it
experiments.verdict: the host OVERWRITES the encoder gradient with g_base + w_b/valid_levels * (g'_L1 + g_L2 + g_L3) and never touches the decoder or the codebook gradient, so an auxiliary term that reaches only the encoder is discarded in production however healthy it looks in isolation; only a term that delivers gradient to the codebook can change the exported SIDs

predictions.falsifier: the encoder gradient after the host's assembly differs from the control's by a nonzero amount
predictions.measurement: a matched pair on the host's mini case: the encoder gradient with and without the term, before and after the host's own projection
predictions.statement: on the host's own mini case, an auxiliary term changes the encoder gradient before the host's assembly and not at all after it

explanations.statement: the host overwrites the encoder gradient after the backward, so an auxiliary term that reaches only the encoder is discarded in production, however healthy it looks in isolation

hypotheses.notes: measured on the host's own code path: the encoder gradient difference is 1.66e-05 before the host's post-backward assembly and exactly 0.0 after it, so the two inert arms' training was bit-identical to the control's. A mechanism that wants to move the exported SIDs has to deliver its gradient to the codebook, which the host never overwrites
hypotheses.observation: two arms' trained models are byte-identical to the matched control's, although their mechanisms pass the independent gradient checks

experiments.result: the delivered codebook gradient scales exactly linearly with the mechanism's weight (0.01 -> 2.961e-02, 0.001 -> 2.961e-03, 0.0001 -> 2.961e-04) and the hard assignment's churn is ZERO at every weight, including the production one
experiments.verdict: E1 is NOT supported: the gradient's magnitude scales, but it does not flip the assignment, so magnitude alone does not explain the collapse

experiments.result: the collapsed arm's codewords moved AWAY from the items they own (level 0: 0.1415 -> 0.2721; level 1: 0.3263 -> 1.4494; level 2: 0.3603 -> 1.6936) while their mutual separation shrank (level 0: 0.3755 -> 0.1272)
experiments.verdict: E2 is REFUTED: the collapse is not a shrinkage toward the items; the used codewords converged onto each other instead

experiments.result: a transition's two level-0 codewords are 0.2732 apart in the control and 0.0644 apart in the collapsed arm (the MEDIAN is 0.0, i.e. the two endpoints share one codeword), and 77.2% of the collapsed arm's pairs sit below a tenth of the control's mean separation against the control's 7.8%
experiments.verdict: E2' is SUPPORTED: the mechanism's codebook gradient pulled the pair's codewords together until the cells merged, and that is the collapse

explanations.statement: the collapse follows the magnitude of the delivered codebook gradient

hypotheses.notes: this closes a line the system was about to take: a cheap screening gate on the level-0 Gini would have refused arms whose cold runs were fine and passed arms whose cold runs concentrated the codes
hypotheses.observation: the screening phase's short probe cannot stand in for the cold run. Across the 19 arms that have both a probe export and a cold export, the probe's paired balance predicts the cold run's balance only weakly (Spearman 0.38 for the level-0 Gini, 0.47 for the number of level-0 codes in use) and the probe's paired enrichment ratio predicts the cold run's ER only weakly (0.51). Gating on that ratio would have wrongly refused an arm whose cold run cleared the gate: directed_assignment_prefix_information has a probe ratio of 0.93 and a cold-run ER of 16.95 against the gate's 16.39.
